title: Markowitz-degree pivot selection for sparse RREF
description:
gf2-core's sparse Gauss-Jordan elimination uses a straight-line column-sweep that doesn't match LinBox's `GaussDomain::NoReordering` pivot-priority strategy. Cross-ratios (sparse-elim × {GF(2), GF(7), GF(251), GF(65521), GF(2^31-1)} at n=256/1024 density 3.9%/0.98%) are uniformly 1.97x-2.61x of LinBox — uniformly outside the 1.5x SOTA contract.

## Background

Per `dev/bench_results/2026-05-04-47698404-sparse-scorecard.md` § 4 *Feasible CPU gaps* and `dev/bench_results/2026-05-08-2cfc4372-sota-scorecard.md` § 4.4, this is an algorithmic gap, not a kernel-tuning gap. LinBox stores priority-queue pivots and does early-out on dependent rows; gf2-core does straight-line sparse Gauss-Jordan.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] Implement Markowitz-degree pivot selection in `SpBitMatrix::rref` (GF(2)) and `SparseFieldMatrix::rref` (GF(p)).
- [hard] Cross-ratios for **7 of the 10** sparse-elim cells (GF(2)/GF(p) × {n=256, n=1024} × scorecard densities) come within 1.5x of LinBox `GaussDomain::NoReordering`. The remaining 3 cells are amended to `[aspirational]` per the user-approved 2026-05-24 amendment below.
- [aspirational] GF(7)/GF(251)/GF(65521) at n=256 (dense regime density=3.9%) deliver at least 1.35x speedup over the pre-Markowitz baseline. Architectural cause: per-pivot O(m) argmin scan + Montgomery REDC per axpy element dominate at small dense n; achievable ratios on the implemented algorithm are 0.516 / 0.604 / 0.627 vs the 0.667 threshold. Closing the residual gap requires lazy-reduction MAC, sparse priority queue, or block elimination — each a separate scoped follow-up.
- [hard] Bit-exact equality vs a canonical Gauss-Jordan reference (the worker's `direct_rref_reference_fp` / `_g8` textbook oracle) — the originally-named `FieldMatrix::rref` dense reference cannot be used because of a separately-discovered pre-existing non-canonical-RREF bug in its PLE path (see follow-up issue).
- [hard] No regression on the existing sparse-rref proptests in `crates/gf2-core/src/sparse.rs::tests`.
- [hard] Filed under epic 97bf0879 umbrella amendment A8 as named follow-up for the 10 sparse-elim FAIL cells documented in `dev/bench_results/2026-05-08-2cfc4372-sota-scorecard.md` § 4.4.

## Amendment — 2026-05-24 (user-approved)

Original criterion 2 required all 10 sparse-elim cells to reach within 1.5× of LinBox. Empirical 5-trial CCX1-pinned measurement post-Markowitz delivers:

| Field | n | ratio (gf2/LinBox) | speedup vs pre | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| GF(2) | 256 | 0.782 | 1.68× | [hard] PASS |
| GF(2) | 1024 | 0.745 | 1.65× | [hard] PASS |
| GF(7) | 256 | 0.516 | 1.35× | [aspirational] |
| GF(7) | 1024 | 0.669 | 1.56× | [hard] PASS |
| GF(251) | 256 | 0.604 | 1.42× | [aspirational] |
| GF(251) | 1024 | 0.749 | 1.60× | [hard] PASS |
| GF(65521) | 256 | 0.627 | 1.43× | [aspirational] |
| GF(65521) | 1024 | 0.791 | 1.56× | [hard] PASS |
| GF(2^31-1) | 256 | 0.720 | 1.54× | [hard] PASS |
| GF(2^31-1) | 1024 | 0.857 | 1.76× | [hard] PASS |

Architectural cause for the 3 [aspirational] cells (GF(7)/GF(251)/GF(65521) at n=256): all GF(p) at the smaller-n + denser regime where per-pivot O(m) argmin scan and Montgomery REDC per axpy element dominate. All 3 deliver 1.35×-1.43× speedup over pre-Markowitz baseline; closing the residual 0.04–0.15 gap to the 1.5× threshold requires a separate optimisation pass (lazy-reduction MAC, sparse priority queue, or block elimination at small n). Same architectural pattern as 27bb2f75's small-n dispatch overhead (closed via table-lookup pack/unpack for n=64 dense GEMM).

User-approved amendment recorded at session-2 close, 2026-05-24. Aggregate contract: 7/10 cells [hard] PASS; 3/10 cells [aspirational] PASS at 1.35×-1.43× speedup over pre-Markowitz baseline (all 10 cells improved by Markowitz).

Evidence: `dev/bench_results/2026-05-24-5ce13bae-markowitz-sparse-rref.md` § 5.
